question: GnRH (gonadotropin-releasing hormone) analogues are the treatment of choice for central (gonadotropin-dependent) precocious puberty because they suppress the HPG axis and halt further pubertal progression.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This is true. GnRH analogues are the first-line treatment for central (true, gonadotropin-dependent) precocious puberty. Peripheral (pseudo-precocious) puberty — driven by autonomous sex steroid secretion — requires treatment of the underlying cause, not GnRH analogues.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. GnRH analogues (e.g. leuprolide) work by continuously stimulating GnRH receptors, causing receptor downregulation and suppression of LH and FSH secretion. This halts premature secondary sexual development, slows bone-age advancement, and may improve final adult height.
